newsitem.title: UK: United rebounds as market rules out bid.
newsitem.headline: United rebounds as market rules out bid.

text.p: Shares in United News & Media rebounded in early trading on Tuesday, bucking a weaker trend in the FTSE 100, as the market ruled out the British information services concern as a bidder for Blenheim Group, traders said.
At 0920 GMT, United News shares were up 23p to 682-1/2p.
United News shares, dragged down recently by talk that it would bid for Blenheim, have fallen almost 10 percent during last month, even as the FTSE 100 advanced to record levels.

"The stock has been a very bad performer, but now there's talk that United News is not going to get involved (in making an bid for Blenheim) and the share price has bounced back on that," said one market maker.
Earlier, brokers for NatWest, acting for a large European media company, bought 14.9 percent of Blenheim, market sources said. But the stakebuilding was not a prelude to a bid, they added.
There was talk in the market yesterday that Reed-Elsevier, whose shares were off 5-1/2p to 1177-1/2p, was poised to launch a bid for Blenheim.
Shares in Blenheim surged to 474p, up 38-1/2p, adding to yesterday's 22p rise.
